name: Site of Xanadu
description: On the grasslands of Inner Mongolia, north of the Great Wall, lie the ruins of Shangdu, the Xanadu of Marco Polo's tales and Coleridge's poem. Kublai Khan's summer capital, laid out in 1256, spreads across 25,000 hectares. Visitors can trace the remains of palaces, temples, tombs, nomad campsites and canal works, all placed by feng shui principles between mountains and river.
